summary: In Greek mythology, Stichius (Ancient Greek Στιχίος) was an Athenian captain under Menestheus at Troy. With Menestheus he carries the fallen Epeian Amphimachus from the field; later he follows among the picked Athenians in the press at the ships. Distinct from the Boeotian Stichius Hector slays in Book 15.

sections.heading: Athenian captain
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 13.195–196, 13.691) pairs Stichius with Menestheus as leaders of the Athenians who bear Amphimachus' body to the Achaean host, and again among the picked men — Pheidas, Stichius, and Bias — who follow Menestheus when the battle thickens at the ships.

Wikipedia's short Stichius article conflates this Athenian with the Boeotian leader of the same name. The atlas keeps them apart: stichius-athenian is Menestheus' comrade in Book 13; he is not the Boeotian Hector lays low beside Arcesilaus in Book 15.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Not stichius-boeotian, the brazen-coated Boeotian captain of Iliad 15.329–331. The shared Wikipedia stub quotes that death-line but applies it to a single merged figure.
